likert.text: Sports is equally important as academic subjects.
likert.notes: Somatic belief: measures valuation of physical balance alongside academics.

likert.text: Sports should be a part of evaluation of grades in your academic result.
likert.notes: Institutional alignment: support for holistic grading vs pure rote tests.

likert.text: You feel that if your favorite game is part of exam then you will top this exam?
likert.notes: Playfulness & passion: captures intrinsic energy and recreational drive.

likert.text: You can play your favorite sports without any time bound?
likert.notes: Autonomous recreation: willingness to play without rigid schedule constraints.

likert.text: You cannot assume your life without sports?
likert.notes: Recreational identity: sports as an essential non-negotiable life pillar.

likert.text: Do you plan to continue participating in sports activities in the future?
likert.notes: Future somatic commitment: intent to sustain exercise throughout college.

likert.text: Have you ever received encouragement or support from your peers or instructors to participate in sports activities?
likert.notes: Peer/faculty sports encouragement: social support for physical wellness.

likert.text: How important do you think promoting sports culture is in educational institutions?
likert.notes: Institutional sports climate: perceived institutional focus on health.

likert.text: rate your interest in participating in sports activities.
likert.notes: Self-rated sports enthusiasm: baseline recreational motivation level.

likert.text: How often do you engage in sports activities?
likert.notes: Physical exercise frequency: concrete behavioral manifestation of fitness.

likert.text: Your parents forcefully admitted you in the engineering?
likert.notes: CRITICAL: Parental coercion in engineering choice. Strongest early-dropout driver!

likert.text: You don’t know why you are studying all these things and didn’t enjoy?
likert.notes: Academic anhedonia: lack of conceptual enjoyment and perceived study futility.

likert.text: You want to get a job so that you can go in some another interest course?
likert.notes: Escapist career intent: viewing degree merely as a bridge to unrelated courses.

likert.text: This course is your favorite.
likert.notes: Intrinsic passion: genuine interest in the engineering curriculum.

likert.text: You see your career in this field only?
likert.notes: Long-term professional vision: commitment to engineering career trajectory.

likert.text: The resources (labs, equipment, software) required for your engineering studies are easily accessible
likert.notes: Perceived resource adequacy: lab equipment, computing, and software accessibility.

likert.text: How often do you collaborate with peers on engineering projects or studies?
likert.notes: Peer technical collaboration: active engagement in engineering project teams.

likert.text: your instructors are supportive in guiding and encouraging your interest in engineering?
likert.notes: Faculty mentorship support: accessibility of instructors for technical guidance.

likert.text: You plan to pursue a career in engineering after graduation?
likert.notes: Post-graduation engineering aspiration: persistence into technical industry.

likert.text: You feel confident in identifying engineering problems and developing effective solutions?
likert.notes: Engineering problem-solving self-efficacy: confidence in designing solutions.

likert.text: You want to study but you don’t know where to start?
likert.notes: Executive dysfunction: cognitive paralysis on where to initiate study.

likert.text: You don’t get interest in study because you think that whenever new semester will start then only you will study?
likert.notes: Chronic semester-delay rationalization: postponing study until next semester.

likert.text: You feel that other students are very intelligent?
likert.notes: Imposter Syndrome: feeling peers are inherently superior/more intelligent.

likert.text: In a semester so many times you make your schedule of study.
likert.notes: Intention-action gap: repeated attempts to formulate study timetables.

likert.text: After each semester you feel very guilty that you didn’t gave your 100%?
likert.notes: Post-semester guilt cycle: chronic regret over suboptimal effort investment.

likert.text: You are confident in setting and achieving your personal and academic goals?
likert.notes: Goal self-efficacy: confidence in setting and executing academic milestones.

likert.text: You are   confident in social interactions with peers and instructors?
likert.notes: Social self-efficacy: ease in interacting with professors and peer classmates.

likert.text: rate your agreement with the statement: "I have high self-esteem."
likert.notes: Global self-esteem: Rosenburg-style self-worth and intellectual confidence.

likert.text: You have some past experiences (failures or successes) that influenced your current level of self-confidence?
likert.notes: Attributional resilience: learning from past setbacks without ego collapse.

likert.text: you are comfortable with trying new activities or taking on new challenges.
likert.notes: Novelty challenge tolerance: comfort with new, open-ended technical tasks.

likert.text: You believe in friendship very much?
likert.notes: Relational valuation: importance placed on collegiate peer friendships.

likert.text: Your friends are same as you in each manner either in study or other things?
likert.notes: Peer homophily: perceived similarity with peer circle in study and values.

likert.text: Your most of the time is spend with your friends?
likert.notes: Social immersion: volume of daily waking hours spent with friend group.

likert.text: You want to spend your time with your friends only in vacations also?
likert.notes: Peer dependency: desire to remain with college friends during vacation.

likert.text: Rate your agreement with the statement: "My friends have a positive influence on my academic and personal life."
likert.notes: Positive peer scaffolding: constructive influence on academic discipline.

likert.text: How often do your friends distract you from your studies?
likert.notes: Toxic peer distraction: friends actively pulling student away from study.

likert.text: you feel pressured by your friends to engage in activities that you are uncomfortable with?
likert.notes: Coercive peer pressure: feeling compelled to engage in uncomfortable acts.

likert.text: the approval of your friends is important   in your decision-making process.
likert.notes: External social approval dependency: inability to make independent choices.

likert.text: do you participate in risky behaviors due to influence from friends?
likert.notes: Peer-induced risk-taking: reckless behavior driven by social conformity.

likert.text: you feel your friends impact your mental health?
likert.notes: Relational mental strain: emotional distress and toxicity in peer group.

likert.text: rate your agreement with the statement: "I am generally in good health."
likert.notes: General physical health status: self-rated biological vitality baseline.

likert.text: How does the quality and variety of food available to you impact your overall well-being in college?
likert.notes: Campus nutritional adequacy: impact of mess food variety on well-being.

likert.text: How often do you eat meals in the campus dining halls or other food facilities?
likert.notes: Campus dining regularity: consistency of eating meals in hostel mess.

likert.text: How often do you engage in physical activity or exercise?
likert.notes: Routine physical exercise: frequency of cardiovascular workout/sports.

likert.text: How would you rate your overall physical and mental health?
likert.notes: Holistic health perception: combined physical and mental vitality score.

likert.text: do you experience health-related issues that affect your daily activities?
likert.notes: Somatic disability: health ailments directly interfering with daily routine.

likert.text: do health issues affect your academic performance?
likert.notes: Health-induced academic decline: medical issues causing low exam scores.

likert.text: do you feel supported by friends, family, and instructors when dealing with health issues?
likert.notes: Health support network: perceived care from family/friends during sickness.

likert.text: You never like mess food?
likert.notes: Mess food aversion: chronic dissatisfaction with campus residential dining.

likert.text: All the time you feel very tired and lazy.
likert.notes: Chronic fatigue syndrome: feeling lethargic, unrefreshed, and exhausted.

likert.text: This environment doesn’t suit you.
likert.notes: Environmental mismatch: feeling the collegiate institutional climate is toxic.

likert.text: At home you are very energetic but not in college?
likert.notes: Home-campus energy divergence: energetic at home but depleted at college.

likert.text: You don’t get good sleep?
likert.notes: Nocturnal sleep deficiency: inability to attain deep, restorative sleep.

likert.text: Your parents always want you to improve more and never satisfies with your performance?
likert.notes: Parental perfectionism: parents never satisfied with academic marks.

likert.text: How satisfied are you with the resources available on campus for managing and coping with family pressure?
likert.notes: Campus coping resources: awareness of institutional counseling for stress.

likert.text: How does Family stress or difficulty impact your academic performance and well-being?
likert.notes: Family conflict spillover: domestic problems impairing concentration.

likert.text: Your parents never motivate you like other parents?
likert.notes: Comparative parental criticism: feeling parents compare student unfavorably.

likert.text: Have you ever discussed this pressure with your family or anyone else for support?
likert.notes: Family emotional dialogue: willingness to discuss stress openly with parents.

likert.text: You never achieve the expectations of your parents?
likert.notes: Chronic failure feeling: perceived permanent inability to meet expectations.

likert.text: You don’t want to talk your parents?
likert.notes: CRITICAL: Parental emotional estrangement. Reluctance to speak to parents.

likert.text: You think that your parents don’t support you like other parents do?
likert.notes: Perceived lack of parental support: feeling isolated compared to peers.

likert.text: do you feel your parents' aspirations influence your own life goals and ambitions?
likert.notes: Parental vicarious ambition: parental goals substituting personal drive.

likert.text: rate your agreement with the statement: "I feel pressure from my family to meet certain expectations."
likert.notes: Family expectation burden: acute pressure to attain high-paying placements.

likert.text: rate your agreement with the statement: "I frequently engage in activities that I consider to be bad habits."
likert.notes: Self-acknowledged bad habits: engaging in addictive or harmful routines.

likert.text: How effective have interventions (counseling, support groups, therapy) been in helping you manage or quit your bad habits?
likert.notes: Therapeutic intervention efficacy: responsiveness to past counseling.

likert.text: You enjoy the late-night parties with your friends?
likert.notes: Nocturnal partying: late-night escapism disrupting circadian rhythms.

likert.text: How do you feel about the resources available on campus for addressing bad habits or addiction?
likert.notes: Campus de-addiction awareness: perception of university counseling support.

likert.text: How has your academic performance been impacted by any bad habits or addiction?
likert.notes: Habit-induced academic damage: performance collapse due to addictions.

likert.text: Study is your first priority in exams.
likert.notes: Exam priority focus: placing academic study above social distractions.

likert.text: If you get less score in exams, your friends are the main reason of your less score?
likert.notes: External locus of control: blaming peer group for personal low marks.

likert.text: Your daily routine is not fix?
likert.notes: Circadian chaos: complete lack of structured daily study/sleep schedule.

likert.text: rate your agreement with the statement: "I frequently feel homesick."
likert.notes: Acute homesickness frequency: persistent emotional pull toward home.

likert.text: You visit home as often as you can?
likert.notes: Frequent home transit: fleeing campus on weekends, hurting study groups.

likert.text: How satisfied are you with the resources available on campus for addressing homesickness?
likert.notes: Campus transition support: satisfaction with institutional orientation.

likert.text: How often do you stay in touch with family and friends from home?
likert.notes: Home contact frequency: healthy communication with family support system.

likert.text: You hardly ever think about home?
likert.notes: Campus independence: emotional stability without compulsive home longing.

likert.text: You call your family so many times during a day?
likert.notes: Compulsive parental calling: calling home multiple times daily due to anxiety.

likert.text: You hate this place?
likert.notes: CRITICAL: Acute institutional rejection. Stating 'You hate this place'.

likert.text: You are very excited when vocation is there?
likert.notes: Vacation fixation: mental disengagement from campus during semester.

likert.text: How significantly does homesickness affect your mental health?
likert.notes: Homesickness psychological toll: homesickness inducing depressive affect.

likert.text: How actively do you participate in campus activities to feel more connected?
likert.notes: Campus activity engagement: participating in clubs to build belonging.

likert.text: You spend so much time on your mobile?
likert.notes: Excessive screen time: compulsive hours spent on mobile devices.

likert.text: your academic performance has been impacted by any Social media addiction?
likert.notes: Social media academic impairment: grades declining due to online apps.

likert.text: Without any message also you scroll down the screen of your mobile for social media.
likert.notes: Phantom scrolling: mindlessly scrolling feeds even without notifications.

likert.text: You cannot assume your life without social media sites or apps?
likert.notes: Digital dependency: expressing life is unimaginable without social apps.

likert.text: Your friends comment on your photo or story matter for you a lot?
likert.notes: Social validation addiction: excessive anxiety over post likes/comments.

likert.text: You share every happy and sad moment with your friends by posting?
likert.notes: Compulsive life broadcasting: sharing every emotional event online.

likert.text: How significantly does your use of mobile phones or social media affect your physical health (e.g., eye strain, posture problems)?
likert.notes: Digital somatic toll: eye strain, neck posture, and physical discomfort.

likert.text: rate your agreement with the statement: "My use of mobile phones or social media disrupts my daily life and activities."
likert.notes: Daily routine disruption: screen time delaying meals, study, and sleep.

likert.text: How often does your use of mobile phones or social media negatively impact your academic performance?
likert.notes: Study distraction: social media interrupts homework and revision.

likert.text: How significantly does your use of mobile phones or social media affect your productivity in academic or personal tasks?
likert.notes: Cognitive productivity decline: inability to sustain deep focused work.

likert.text: Have you ever tried to reduce your use of mobile phones or social media?
likert.notes: Failed digital detox: attempted reduction of phone usage and failed.

likert.text: How anxious do you feel when you are unable to access your mobile phone or social media?
likert.notes: Nomophobia & withdrawal: severe anxiety when mobile access is denied.

likert.text: How often do you use your mobile phone or social media during classes or study sessions?
likert.notes: In-class digital distraction: using smartphone apps during live lectures.

likert.text: Are you sleeping more or less then you normally sleep?
likert.notes: Sleep architecture disruption: insomnia or excessive vegetative hypersomnia.

likert.text: Do you feel tired, no matter how much you sleep?
likert.notes: Unrefreshing sleep: persistent exhaustion regardless of sleep duration.

likert.text: Are you enjoying the things right now happening in your life?
likert.notes: Anhedonia marker: ability to experience joy in current daily events.

likert.text: You don’t like interaction with anybody?
likert.notes: Social withdrawal & isolation: aversion to interacting with all humans.

likert.text: Have you noticed any changes in your physical appearance, such as bloodshot eyes, unusual odors, or sudden weight loss or gain in the past month?
likert.notes: Somatic physical breakdown: bloodshot eyes, drastic weight fluctuations.

likert.text: It is difficult for you to talk with your friends also.
likert.notes: Relational shutdown: inability to converse even with closest friends.

likert.text: Have you noticed any changes in your sleeping patterns or appetite recently?
likert.notes: Vegetative somatic shifts: acute appetite loss or erratic circadian shifts.

likert.text: Have you noticed any changes in your academic performance or behavior, such as missing classes or assignments, arriving late, or engaging in disruptive behavior in the past month?
likert.notes: Behavioral disinhibition: unexcused absenteeism, chronic late arrivals.

likert.text: How often have you felt disoriented or confused in the past month?
likert.notes: CRITICAL: Cognitive disorientation, severe confusion, and acute crisis.

AM.name: Academic Motivation
AM.desc: Autonomous academic purpose, intrinsic drive, and rejection of forced enrollment.

ASE.name: Academic Self-Efficacy
ASE.desc: Confidence in mastering complex technical coursework and solving engineering challenges.

EI.name: Engineering Identity
EI.desc: Intrinsic alignment with the engineering profession and seeing long-term career in tech.

GM.name: Growth Mindset
GM.desc: Perception of intelligence as expandable, viewing academic setbacks as learning inputs.

TM.name: Time Management
TM.desc: Deliberate scheduling, proactive milestone tracking, and resisting nocturnal study chaos.

SRC.name: Study Consistency
SRC.desc: Daily revision discipline, absence of start-stop cycles, and sustained study momentum.

PRM.name: Procrastination Management
PRM.desc: Overcoming assignment delays, task paralysis, and post-exam regret.

MM.name: Metacognitive Regulation
MM.desc: Self-monitoring of learning comprehension and calibrating study effort to performance.

AAR.name: Academic Test Anxiety
AAR.desc: Tolerance of timed high-stakes exams and cognitive calm during assessments.

SQCR.name: Sleep Quality & Circadian Rhythm
SQCR.desc: Consistent 7+ hour circadian schedule, nocturnal rhythm regularity, and low fatigue.

SCR.name: Stress Coping Resilience
SCR.desc: Adaptive coping under engineering workload, low substance reliance, and emotional recovery.

PAW.name: Physical Activity & Somatics
PAW.desc: Sports engagement, somatic energy, physical fitness, and mess food adaptation.

SDA.name: Screen Time & Digital Focus
SDA.desc: Controlled mobile screen time, resistance to in-class phone distraction and doomscrolling.

BEL.name: Campus Belonging & Transition
BEL.desc: Hostel community adjustment, overcoming homesickness and relocation shock.

PCL.name: Peer Group Collaboration
PCL.desc: Study group participation, collaborative homework, and resilience to negative peer influence.

FAM.name: Family Autonomy & Low Coercion
FAM.desc: Freedom from hyper-critical parental perfectionism, comparative pressure, and guilt.

FSI.name: Faculty Seeking & Guidance
FSI.desc: Proactive instructor consultation, attending office hours, and counseling openness.

CS.name: Clinical Distress Safety Screener
CS.desc: Screening for severe somatic exhaustion, vegetative disruption, disorientation, and acute crisis.
